title: Affinity-led kernel arbitration and prefetch SLO simulator
creator: Sasha Kim
description:
Problem: Our current kernel selection and prefetch admission logic favors throughput at the cost of bursty latency for small interactive requests that share KV pages. This surface causes tail latency spikes when a low-affinity kernel is selected or when prefetch admission triggers expensive page loads during decode.

Goal: Prototype and validate an affinity-aware arbitration layer that combines per-request kernel affinity signals, recent KV-page telemetry, and a prefetch admission controller. Build an SLO-focused simulator to measure trade-offs across latency tail, overall throughput, and token cost before we change production routing.

Scope: This ticket covers design, a lightweight simulator, controlled bench experiments on a cluster replica, and a runbook for a limited canary rollout. It does not include full rollout of a new scheduler or deep kernel rewrite — that will be separate once the simulation and bench results justify changes.

Deliverables:
- Design doc describing affinity signals, scoring function, and prefetch admission rules.
- SLO simulator that consumes request traces and replica KV telemetry and outputs latency/throughput/cost trade-offs for candidate policies.
- Bench harness running representative workloads (interactive chat vs batch generation) to validate simulator predictions.
- PRD-style rollout plan with metrics, rollback criteria, and observability hooks.

Success criteria: simulator predictions align with bench results within 10% for median/tail latencies, and a chosen policy reduces 99th percentile decode latency by >= 15% on interactive workloads without >5% token-cost regression.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by runtime and infra leads (link to doc in comments).
SLO simulator implemented and documented with public input format and example traces.
Bench harness reproduces at least two workload profiles and produces comparable metrics to the simulator (median + p90 + p99 latencies, tokens/sec, and additional token cost).
At least one candidate policy reduces p99 decode latency by >= 15% on interactive trace in bench without >5% token-cost increase, or simulation explains tradeoffs if target not met.
Rollout plan created with clear observability dashboards and rollback thresholds.
design_notes: Affinity signals considered: model variant, sequence length distribution, recent KV page touch frequency, kernel hotness score, and tenant priority.
Scoring function will produce a kernel affinity score in [-1,1] with thresholds driving 'prefer-local-kernel', 'allow-mixed', and 'defer-prefetch' decisions.

Prefetch admission controller should be conservative by default: only permit prefetch for requests where expected downstream decode savings exceed the admission cost estimate by a configurable margin.
Telemetry inputs: per-page last-touch timestamp, resident fraction, kernel busy ratio, and realtime decode queue depth. Need small schema extension (see comment linking telemetry RFC).
bench_plan: Replay anonymized production traces from 2026-02 with 3 workload slices: low-latency chat, bursty batch, long-context summarization.
Run each policy variant 10x on a dedicated bench cluster to control noise (use same seed for RNGs where applicable).
Measure median/p90/p99 decode latency, tokens/sec, average token cost, and KV page fault rate.
Collect kernel scheduling logs and KV telemetry for post-hoc correlation analysis.
simulator_details: Input: time-ordered request traces (timestamp, model, seq_len, tenant_id, hint_flags) and snapshot-style KV telemetry samples (per-page resident_frac, last_touch).
Policy primitives: affinity_score(request, page_set), prefetch_admit(request, page_set), kernel_select(request, affinity_score), backpressure_rules(queue_depths).
Outputs: latency distribution estimates, estimated token cost, expected prefetch-induced page loads, and simulated kernel queue utilization.
Implementation note: start with deterministic discrete-event simulator in Go/Python; keep components pluggable for future RL-based tuning.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: simulator underestimates variance from hardware noise. Mitigation: run bench experiments and add noise model to simulator; conservatively widen rollout thresholds.
Risk: telemetry schema changes increase control plane load. Mitigation: sample telemetry and use low-cardinality aggregates for admission decisions.
Risk: policy overfits to sampled traces. Mitigation: cross-validate across multiple trace slices and runholdout tenant tests in bench.
